records.issue_text: Cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin uses literal alias "alias" instead of the actual created aliases ("idp-alias-" + i and "idp-alias-20"), making cleanup a no-op and leaking 20+ IDPs into the realm, breaking other tests and re-runs
records.rationale: In `testCacheIDPForLogin`, after creating each IDP with alias `"idp-alias-" + i`, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (and again for `idp-alias-20`). This hard-coded lookup key `"alias"` does not match the created aliases, so the cleanup likely removes nothing, leaking the created IDPs into the realm and potentially impacting subsequent tests/reruns.

records.issue_text: Duplicated invalidation loop: registerIDPLoginInvalidation and registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate both contain identical FetchMode.values() registration loop that will drift; should extract invalidateLoginCaches() helper
records.rationale:
The diff shows two separate methods that both hardcode the same invalidation loop:
- `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(...)`: `for (FetchMode mode : FetchMode.values()) { realmCache.registerInvalidation(cacheKeyForLogin(getRealm(), mode)); }`
- `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate(...)`: same loop in its final branch.
This duplication is verifiable and creates a concrete maintainability/drift risk (e.g., if invalidation logic or cache keying ever changes, it must be updated consistently in two places), though it is not a correctness defect by itself.

records.issue_text: NPE risk in new predicate: idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC) throws NPE if getConfig() returns null
records.rationale: The diff adds a new condition to the login predicate: `.and(idp -> idp.getOrganizationId() == null || Boolean.parseBoolean(idp.getConfig().get(OrganizationModel.BROKER_PUBLIC)))`. If `idp.getOrganizationId() != null` and `idp.getConfig()` is `null`, then `idp.getConfig().get(...)` will throw an NPE. The diff does not show any null-guard or guarantee that `getConfig()` is non-null for all `IdentityProviderModel` instances, so this is a real NPE risk introduced by the change.
